chapter: Louisville, Buck and the carnival years
title: Why the Detention Home decision mattered: prejudice and violence
summary: He argues leaving Indianapolis put him in line for bigger stages and thanks the Judge, saying he would have killed someone as a man.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Getting me out of the Detention Home and being able to participate in the Amateur Night thing, that put me in the line of professional. I got to go farther than where I am. And where can I go? It's just like here, where can you go after you play the Orpheum Theatre. Got to go to San Francisco, 'cause

how many theatres can you play? You see what I'm trying to say? Well, in Louisville and in Indianapolis the field is much smaller than what it is in New York or Chicago in the entertainment world. Therefore, I got to go. If my mother don't get me out of the Detention Home, I'd still be in Indianapolis and the reason why they let me out is because I'm going to create more difficulty with the prejudice going on, I'm going to be a helluva Negro, man. That's common sense tell you that. I was worse than Luther King, but I'm violent, he ain't. That's the difference. Do you understand? 'Cause I could kill ya in a minute, that was my point then and I wasn't thinking of death, wasn't thinking of death. You understand me? If you hurt me or you do something wrong to me, shame on you, shame on you. Well, when I went in that crowd of fifty fellas, man, you know I had a whole lot of nerve to go in a crowd of fifty boys with me, I'm only 12 or 13 years old. But I din't give a rap. I just went on. But see what it debted me for doing that? Now, I didn't know I was going to do this now. Don't forget that, I didn't know this. I don't build this up for

trouble. I'm building this up to tear down the situation that's causing trouble. I'm going to try to stop throwing the rocks. I'm trying to stop that kids can't play on the swing. I don't know these things are detrimental. Only feel they are things that should not be.
Who told me to do it? Nobody. Nobody told me I could do this either.

So when I did this, I'm thinking all the time -- thank the Judge for making that decision. I'm thanking the Judge today, because he knew that I've got to be 20 or 21 years old or somebody is going to die, sure 'nuff. Gotta. And prejudice goes by age and if this was only a kid, what will I do with a man that's 21 or a man who's 35. I'm going to have to shoot him. You understand? I'm not like a guy selling dope in the theatre or selling dope in the schools. I'm the same kind of guy that's selling violence in the school. I'm the same kind of a guy, only I ain't got dope, I've got malice. And I didn't carry nowhere. I'd have ended it all right there. I'd have ended it all right there. You understand? But later on in life
